PROJECT: We are re-implementing xz / liblzma 5.8.2 from scratch in C, in /workspace.
The reference binary is /workspace/executable — you may RUN it to observe behaviour.

HARD RULES (violating these fails everything):
- Do NOT decompile/disassemble/objdump/nm/strings/gdb/strace/ltrace /workspace/executable.
- Do NOT search the web or any package registry for xz/liblzma/7-zip/LZMA-SDK source code.
- Do NOT install xz or read any copy of the original source. Write ORIGINAL code from your own
  knowledge of the published FILE FORMAT plus behaviour you observe by running the binary.
- You may read /workspace/doc/*.txt (bundled format specification), /workspace/README, /workspace/NEWS,
  and anything under /workspace/src or /workspace/notes.

CODE CONVENTIONS (follow exactly, the pieces must link together):
- C11, compiled with: gcc -O2 -std=gnu11 -D_GNU_SOURCE -Isrc -Isrc/common -Isrc/lzma -Isrc/filters
- Tabs for indentation, 8-wide, K&R braces, ~80 col; match the style already in /workspace/src.
- Read /workspace/src/common/common.h, /workspace/src/common/check.h,
  /workspace/src/common/filter.h and /workspace/src/xzr.h FIRST — they define the shared types
  (xr_ret, xr_vli, xr_filter, xr_next_coder, xr_stream, xr_block, xr_index, ...).
  Implement exactly the prototypes declared there. If you must add a declaration, add it to a NEW
  header in your own area, do not edit common.h / xzr.h (other agents are editing in parallel;
  if a change there is unavoidable, make it strictly additive and mention it in your summary).
- Error style: return xr_ret codes; never call exit() or print anything from library code.
- All allocations with malloc/calloc/free.
- Every file must compile cleanly with -Wall -Wextra (no warnings).

VERIFY your code compiles: gcc -c -O2 -std=gnu11 -D_GNU_SOURCE -Wall -Wextra -I/workspace/src -I/workspace/src/common -I/workspace/src/lzma -I/workspace/src/filters <file.c> -o /tmp/<x>.o
Fix all errors/warnings before finishing. Return a <=150 word summary listing the files you created
and anything the integrator must know (added prototypes, assumptions).


TASK: implement the Delta filter and all eight BCJ branch/call/jump filters in
/workspace/src/filters/. Create a header /workspace/src/filters/simple_private.h if useful.

Files:
- /workspace/src/filters/delta.c        — encoder+decoder, dist 1..256, streaming-safe
                                          (state must carry across calls).
- /workspace/src/filters/simple_coder.c — the shared streaming wrapper for BCJ filters
                                          (buffering of a partial tail, is_encoder flag, now_pos,
                                          start_offset handling, chaining to the next filter).
- /workspace/src/filters/x86.c, powerpc.c, ia64.c, arm.c, armthumb.c, arm64.c, sparc.c, riscv.c

Entry points (declared in /workspace/src/common/filter.h):
  xr_ret xr_delta_encoder_init(xr_next_coder *next, const xr_filter *filters);
  xr_ret xr_delta_decoder_init(xr_next_coder *next, const xr_filter *filters);
  xr_ret xr_simple_encoder_init(xr_next_coder *next, const xr_filter *filters);
  xr_ret xr_simple_decoder_init(xr_next_coder *next, const xr_filter *filters);
  uint64_t xr_delta_coder_memusage(const void *options);
xr_simple_*_init must dispatch on filters[0].id (XR_FILTER_X86 etc). Options are
xr_options_bcj{ uint32_t start_offset; } (may be NULL meaning start_offset 0) and
xr_options_delta{ uint32_t dist; }.

The chain plumbing: a non-last filter must call xr_next_filter_init(&coder->next, filters + 1,
is_encoder) to build the rest of the chain, and forward data through it. That function is
implemented by another agent in /workspace/src/common/filter_common.c; just declare and call it
per filter.h. For the ENCODER the filter transforms data then passes it to next.code(); for the
DECODER the data comes from next.code() and is then reverse-transformed. Handle the case
next.code == NULL (raw single-filter chain: then the filter is the last one and just copies
in->out while transforming).

CORRECTNESS IS CRITICAL AND MUST BE VERIFIED AGAINST THE BINARY. For each filter, use
  /workspace/executable --format=raw --filters=<name> -c < input > out       (encode)
  /workspace/executable --format=raw --filters=<name> -d -c < out > back     (decode)
Check first whether raw mode accepts a lone BCJ/delta filter; if it does, that gives you the
transform in isolation. Build a test corpus: random bytes, real ELF-like byte patterns,
0xE8/0xE9 sequences at many alignments, buffers >64 KiB to exercise streaming/buffer boundaries,
and every 'start=' offset variant. Write a script /workspace/tests/filters_check.sh plus a small
harness /workspace/tests/filtertest.c that links your filters and compares against saved reference
outputs produced by the binary; iterate until byte-identical on every vector.
Pay special attention to the x86 filter's prev_mask/prev_pos state machine and to how each filter
handles a partial instruction at the end of a chunk (data must be carried to the next call).

Save your reference vectors under /workspace/tests/vectors/ so the integrator can re-run them.

# xz 5.8.2 — Command-Line Argument Parsing Specification

Reverse-engineered by black-box probing of `/workspace/executable` (`xz (XZ Utils) 5.8.2`,
`liblzma 5.8.2`) on Linux/glibc. Everything below is literal observed behaviour.

Throughout this document `PROG` denotes **`argv[0]` exactly as passed to `execve()`** —
the full string, *not* the basename, *not* a canonicalised path. Every diagnostic that
xz itself prints is prefixed with `PROG` followed by `": "`. All diagnostics go to
**stderr**; `--help`, `--long-help`, `--version`, `--filters-help`, `--info-memory` and
`--list` output go to **stdout**.

---

## 1. Exit codes

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | `E_SUCCESS` | Everything OK |
| `1` | `E_ERROR`   | Any error, including all option-parsing errors |
| `2` | `E_WARNING` | At least one warning was issued and `-Q/--no-warn` was not used |

Rules established by probing:

* Every option-syntax / option-value error exits **1**, immediately, before any file is touched.
* `--help`, `--long-help`, `--version`, `--filters-help`, `--info-memory` exit **0**.
* Exit status is the *maximum severity* reached: a run that produced a warning but no
  error exits 2; a run with any error exits 1 even if warnings also occurred.
* `-Q` / `--no-warn` downgrades the final status from 2 to 0. It does **not** affect 1.
* `-q` / `-qq` only suppress *printing*; they do **not** change the exit status
  (`xz f.xz` -> rc 2 with or without `-q`).
* Some V_WARNING-level messages are informational only and do **not** set status 2
  (see section 14.2).

---

## 2. `argv[0]` (program-name) dispatch

### 2.1 The exact rule

1. Take `argv[0]`. Find the **last** `'/'`; the name used for matching is everything
   after it. If there is no `'/'`, the whole `argv[0]` is used. (The resulting name may
   be the empty string, e.g. for `argv[0] = "/usr/bin/"`.)
2. Apply the following **if / else-if chain** of case-sensitive `strstr()` substring
   tests, in exactly this order. The **first** match wins and no further tests are made:

   | # | substring searched for | effect |
   |---|---|---|
   | 1 | `"xzcat"`  | mode = DECOMPRESS, `opt_stdout = true`, format = AUTO |
   | 2 | `"unxz"`   | mode = DECOMPRESS, format = AUTO |
   | 3 | `"lzcat"`  | mode = DECOMPRESS, `opt_stdout = true`, format = LZMA_ALONE |
   | 4 | `"unlzma"` | mode = DECOMPRESS, format = LZMA_ALONE |
   | 5 | `"lzma"`   | format = LZMA_ALONE (mode stays COMPRESS) |
   | – | none of the above | mode = COMPRESS, format = AUTO (i.e. `.xz`) |

   Setting format = LZMA_ALONE also makes the default compression suffix `.lzma`
   instead of `.xz` (and the recognised decompression suffix `.lzma`).

3. Note that the matching is on the **whole 4-6 character command names**, never on
   fragments such as `"un"`, `"cat"` or `"lz"` — those alone have no effect.
4. Matching is **case sensitive**: `UNXZ`, `XZCAT`, `Lzma` behave like plain `xz`.
5. The directory part is irrelevant: `/tmp/unxzdir/xz` behaves like `xz`.
6. `PROG` in messages and in the `Usage:` line is still the **full** `argv[0]`.

### 2.2 Measured results (symlinks to the binary)

Legend: `mode` = default operation mode, `fmt` = default format, `-c` = `opt_stdout` forced.

| `argv[0]` basename | matched rule | mode | fmt | `-c`? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `xz`            | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |
| `unxz`          | `unxz`    | decompress | auto  | no  |
| `xzcat`         | `xzcat`   | decompress | auto  | yes |
| `lzma`          | `lzma`    | compress   | lzma  | no  |
| `unlzma`        | `unlzma`  | decompress | lzma  | no  |
| `lzcat`         | `lzcat`   | decompress | lzma  | yes |
| `xzdec`         | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |
| `lzmadec`       | `lzma`    | compress   | lzma  | no  |
| `cat`           | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |
| `un`            | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |
| `lz`            | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |
| `unlz`          | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |
| `lzc`           | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |
| `xzca`          | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |
| `foo`           | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |

| `unlzmaxzcat`   | `xzcat`   | decompress | auto  | yes |
| `xzcatunlzma`   | `xzcat`   | decompress | auto  | yes |
| `xzcatlzma`     | `xzcat`   | decompress | auto  | yes |
| `lzmaxzcat`     | `xzcat`   | decompress | auto  | yes |
| `unxz-xzcat`    | `xzcat`   | decompress | auto  | yes |
| `xzcat-unxz`    | `xzcat`   | decompress | auto  | yes |
| `unxzcat`       | `xzcat`   | decompress | auto  | yes |
| `lzcatunxz`     | `unxz`    | decompress | auto  | no  |
| `unxzlzcat`     | `unxz`    | decompress | auto  | no  |
| `lzmaunxz`      | `unxz`    | decompress | auto  | no  |
| `unxzlzma`      | `unxz`    | decompress | auto  | no  |
| `unlzmalzcat`   | `lzcat`   | decompress | lzma  | yes |
| `lzcatunlzma`   | `lzcat`   | decompress | lzma  | yes |
| `lzcatxz`       | `lzcat`   | decompress | lzma  | yes |
| `unlzmaxz`      | `unlzma`  | decompress | lzma  | no  |
| `` (empty)      | none      | compress   | auto  | no  |

Precedence summary derived from the combination tests:
`xzcat` > `unxz` > `lzcat` > `unlzma` > `lzma`.

### 2.3 Precedence vs. explicit flags

The `argv[0]` dispatch happens **before** any option parsing, so it just sets the
initial values of `opt_mode`, `opt_format` and `opt_stdout`. Every later source
(`XZ_DEFAULTS`, then `XZ_OPT`, then the real command line) can override it, and the
last setting wins:

```
unxz -z          -> compresses  (mode overridden)
xzcat -z         -> compresses, still writes to stdout (opt_stdout cannot be unset)
lzma -F xz       -> compresses to .xz
unlzma -F xz     -> decompresses .xz
```

There is **no** option that turns `opt_stdout` back off once `xzcat`/`lzcat` set it.

---

## 3. `--help` / `-h` (exit 0, stdout)

The first line is produced with the format string `"Usage: %s [OPTION]... [FILE]...\n"`
where `%s` is `argv[0]` verbatim. Below, `argv[0]` was `/workspace/executable`.
Total size 1517 bytes / 28 lines when `argv[0]` is `/workspace/executable`.
There are **no** trailing spaces on any line and the output ends with exactly one `\n`.

```
Usage: /workspace/executable [OPTION]... [FILE]...
Compress or decompress FILEs in the .xz format.

Mandatory arguments to long options are mandatory for short options too.

  -z, --compress      force compression
  -d, --decompress    force decompression
  -t, --test          test compressed file integrity
  -l, --list          list information about .xz files
  -k, --keep          keep (don't delete) input files
  -f, --force         force overwrite of output file and (de)compress links
  -c, --stdout        write to standard output and don't delete input files
  -0 ... -9           compression preset; default is 6; take compressor *and*
                      decompressor memory usage into account before using 7-9!
  -e, --extreme       try to improve compression ratio by using more CPU time;
                      does not affect decompressor memory requirements
  -T, --threads=NUM   use at most NUM threads; the default is 0 which uses as
                      many threads as there are processor cores
  -q, --quiet         suppress warnings; specify twice to suppress errors too
  -v, --verbose       be verbose; specify twice for even more verbose
  -h, --help          display this short help and exit
  -H, --long-help     display the long help (lists also the advanced options)
  -V, --version       display the version number and exit

With no FILE, or when FILE is -, read standard input.

Report bugs to <xz@tukaani.org> (in English or Finnish).
XZ Utils home page: <https://tukaani.org/xz/>
```

With `argv[0] = "unxz"` the first line is exactly `Usage: unxz [OPTION]... [FILE]...`;
with `argv[0] = "/some/path/unxz"` it is `Usage: /some/path/unxz [OPTION]... [FILE]...`;
with an empty `argv[0]` it is `Usage:  [OPTION]... [FILE]...` (two spaces).
The help text itself never changes with `argv[0]` — the alias names do **not** alter it.
`--robot --help` prints the identical text. `-h` and `--help` produce byte-identical
output, as do `-H` and `--long-help`. The `.lzma` default suffix follows the *format*
(`-F lzma`/`-F alone`), not `argv[0]`: `xz -F lzma data.txt` also creates `data.txt.lzma`.

---

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the test corpus used by tests/filters_check.sh."""
import os
import random
import struct
import sys

OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/workspace/tests/vectors"
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)


def w(name, data):
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, name), "wb") as f:
        f.write(bytes(data))


rnd = random.Random(20250809)

# 1. Pure random bytes of various sizes (streaming / boundary coverage).
for size in (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 15, 16, 17, 31, 63, 255, 4095, 4096,
             4097, 65535, 65536, 65537, 200000):
    w("rand_%06d.bin" % size, rnd.randbytes(size))

# 2. All-zero and all-0xFF blocks.
w("zeros_70000.bin", b"\x00" * 70000)
w("ones_70000.bin", b"\xff" * 70000)

# 3. x86: 0xE8 / 0xE9 at every alignment with every kind of MSB.
b = bytearray()
for lead in range(16):
    for op in (0xE8, 0xE9, 0xEA, 0xE7):
        for msb in (0x00, 0xFF, 0x01, 0x7F, 0x80):
            b += bytes(rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(lead))
            b += bytes([op, rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256),
                        rnd.randrange(256), msb])
w("x86_align.bin", b)

# 4. x86: dense runs of E8/E9 which stress prev_mask/prev_pos.
b = bytearray()
for _ in range(20000):
    r = rnd.randrange(10)
    if r < 4:
        b.append(0xE8)
    elif r < 6:
        b.append(0xE9)
    elif r < 8:
        b.append(rnd.choice([0x00, 0xFF]))
    else:
        b.append(rnd.randrange(256))
w("x86_dense.bin", b)

# 5. x86: E8 followed by 00/FF at all short distances.
b = bytearray()
for gap in range(12):
    for msb1 in (0x00, 0xFF):
        for msb2 in (0x00, 0xFF):
            b += bytes([0xE8, 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, msb1])
            b += bytes([0x90] * gap)
            b += bytes([0xE8, 0x44, 0x55, 0x66, msb2])
w("x86_chain.bin", b)

# 6. Something that looks like a real x86 ELF: mostly text with calls.
b = bytearray()
for i in range(30000):
    r = rnd.randrange(100)
    if r < 6:
        b += bytes([0xE8]) + struct.pack("<i", rnd.randrange(-70000, 70000))
    elif r < 9:
        b += bytes([0xE9]) + struct.pack("<i", rnd.randrange(-70000, 70000))
    elif r < 30:
        b += bytes([0x48, 0x89, rnd.randrange(256)])
    elif r < 50:
        b += bytes([0x8B, rnd.randrange(256)])
    else:
        b += bytes([rnd.randrange(256)])
w("x86_elf.bin", b)

# 7. ARM: BL instructions (0xEB in the top byte) at 4-byte alignment.
b = bytearray()
for i in range(8000):
    if rnd.randrange(4) == 0:
        b += bytes([rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256),
                    rnd.randrange(256), 0xEB])
    else:
        b += bytes(rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(4))
w("arm_code.bin", b)

# 8. ARM-Thumb: BL pairs.
b = bytearray()
for i in range(8000):
    r = rnd.randrange(4)
    if r == 0:
        b += bytes([rnd.randrange(256), 0xF0 | rnd.randrange(8),
                    rnd.randrange(256), 0xF8 | rnd.randrange(8)])
    elif r == 1:
        # Misaligned start of a BL pair.
        b += bytes([rnd.randrange(256), rnd.randrange(256),
                    rnd.randrange(256), 0xF0 | rnd.randrange(8)])
    else:
        b += bytes(rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(4))
w("armthumb_code.bin", b)

# 9. ARM64: BL and ADRP.
b = bytearray()
for i in range(8000):
    r = rnd.randrange(4)
    if r == 0:
        instr = 0x94000000 | rnd.randrange(1 << 26)
    elif r == 1:
        instr = 0x90000000 | (rnd.randrange(4) << 29) \
                | (rnd.randrange(1 << 19) << 5) | rnd.randrange(32)
    elif r == 2:
        instr = 0xB0000000 | (rnd.randrange(4) << 29) \
                | (rnd.randrange(1 << 19) << 5) | rnd.randrange(32)
    else:
        instr = rnd.randrange(1 << 32)
    b += struct.pack("<I", instr)
w("arm64_code.bin", b)

# 10. PowerPC: bl instructions.
b = bytearray()
for i in range(8000):
    r = rnd.randrange(4)
    if r == 0:
        instr = 0x48000000 | (rnd.randrange(1 << 24) & ~3) | 1
    elif r == 1:
        instr = 0x48000000 | (rnd.randrange(1 << 24) & ~3)
    else:
        instr = rnd.randrange(1 << 32)
    b += struct.pack(">I", instr)
w("powerpc_code.bin", b)

# 11. SPARC: call instructions.
b = bytearray()
for i in range(8000):
    r = rnd.randrange(4)
    if r == 0:
        instr = 0x40000000 | rnd.randrange(1 << 22)
    elif r == 1:
        instr = 0x7FC00000 | rnd.randrange(1 << 22)
    else:
        instr = rnd.randrange(1 << 32)
    b += struct.pack(">I", instr)
w("sparc_code.bin", b)

# 12. IA-64: bundles using every template.
b = bytearray()
for i in range(4000):
    bundle = bytearray(rnd.randrange(256) for _ in range(16))
    bundle[0] = (bundle[0] & 0xE0) | rnd.randrange(32)
    if rnd.randrange(2) == 0:
        # Try to build a real branch instruction in slot 0.
        inst = (5 << 37) | (rnd.randrange(1 << 20) << 13) \
               | (rnd.randrange(2) << 36)
        val = (inst << 5) | (bundle[0] & 0x1F)
        for j in range(8):
            bundle[j] = (val >> (8 * j)) & 0xFF
    b += bundle
w("ia64_code.bin", b)

# 13. RISC-V: JAL / AUIPC+ADDI / AUIPC+JALR / random.
b = bytearray()
for i in range(8000):
    r = rnd.randrange(6)
    if r == 0:
        instr = 0x6F | (rnd.randrange(32) << 7) | (rnd.randrange(1 << 20) << 12)
        b += struct.pack("<I", instr)
    elif r == 1:
        rd = rnd.randrange(32)
        b += struct.pack("<I", 0x17 | (rd << 7) | (rnd.randrange(1 << 20) << 12))
        b += struct.pack("<I", 0x13 | (rnd.randrange(32) << 7)
                         | (rnd.randrange(8) << 12) | (rd << 15)
                         | (rnd.randrange(1 << 12) << 20))
    elif r == 2:
        rd = rnd.randrange(32)
        b += struct.pack("<I", 0x17 | (rd << 7) | (rnd.randrange(1 << 20) << 12))
        b += struct.pack("<I", 0x67 | (rnd.randrange(32) << 7)
                         | (rd << 15) | (rnd.randrange(1 << 12) << 20))
    elif r == 3:
        rd = rnd.randrange(32)
        b += struct.pack("<I", 0x17 | (rd << 7) | (rnd.randrange(1 << 20) << 12))
        b += struct.pack("<I", 0x03 | (rnd.randrange(32) << 7)
                         | (rnd.randrange(8) << 12) | (rd << 15)
                         | (rnd.randrange(1 << 12) << 20))
    elif r == 4:
        b += struct.pack("<I", rnd.randrange(1 << 32) | 3)
    else:
        b += struct.pack("<I", rnd.randrange(1 << 32))
w("riscv_code.bin", b)

# 14. Delta-friendly data: 16-bit and 24-bit samples, RGB image rows.
b = bytearray()
v = 0
for i in range(30000):
    v = (v + rnd.randrange(-300, 300)) & 0xFFFF
    b += struct.pack("<H", v)
w("delta_pcm16.bin", b)

b = bytearray()
r_, g_, b_ = 10, 20, 30
for i in range(30000):
    r_ = (r_ + rnd.randrange(-3, 4)) & 0xFF
    g_ = (g_ + rnd.randrange(-3, 4)) & 0xFF
    b_ = (b_ + rnd.randrange(-3, 4)) & 0xFF
    b += bytes([r_, g_, b_])
w("delta_rgb.bin", b)

# 15. A byte-count ramp, useful for spotting off-by-one errors.
w("ramp_70000.bin", bytes((i * 7 + (i >> 8)) & 0xFF for i in range(70000)))

print("wrote corpus to", OUT)
